beats.name: hook
beats.said: A man sold his happiest memory to a stranger at a counter
beats.shown: Jerry at counter, fly-in to glowing memory chip, grinning hooded clerk

beats.name: setup
beats.said: Memories are currency; shops extract them; rent and groceries cost birthdays; wall splits city
beats.shown: Shop, street, storefronts, bicycle kid, wall light shafts

beats.name: explainer
beats.said: Rich buy summers, poor stare at photos; happier memories pay more
beats.shown: Pool, bell-helmet man, bench of elders, happiness gauge

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: Jerry sells one for rent; sick brother begs for frog story; medicine costs more
beats.shown: Night street, hospital bed, polaroid and lake dock, machine

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: He sells summer, birthday, then whole years until his head is bad days
beats.shown: Dark counter, deposit box, hospital hall, BUY SUMMERS street

beats.name: twist
beats.said: One good year left; clerk warns it is empty of happiness; he sells anyway
beats.shown: Ledger of SOLD years, clerk, close-up faces, white glowing chip

beats.name: payoff
beats.said: Brother wakes cured and asks for the frog story; Jerry does not know him
beats.shown: Brother sitting up in bed, Jerry blank face close-up

beats.name: ending
beats.said: Every happy year sold, and the brother was in all of them
beats.shown: Two-shot of brothers in ward, static, blue light

hook.first_frame: Orange-haired Jerry stands at a wooden counter in a dim shop, hooded grinning clerk behind glass at left, green lamp above
hook.first_3s: Slight push-in on Jerry, whip fly-through down to a glowing memory chip on the counter, then swing up to the clerk and shelves of chips
hook.title_vs_first_line: Title 'Every Memory Has a Price' is the theme of the first line; neither repeats the other

story.real_fact_core: Invented world where memories are currency; selling the happiest ones leaves nothing and the loved person is erased from memory.
story.explainer_turn: "You see" at 3.4 s, then present-tense world rules
story.ending_type: twist reveal is the last line

tone.humour: Dark with light gag touches (Bahamas 300 times from a couch, frog size of a football)
tone.deadpan_or_irony: Deadpan delivery; irony in the cure erasing the brother
tone.dialogue_style: Two short quoted lines, brother asks for the frog story; clerk warns
